name: Y2K Design. This is a supplemental design reference and is not claimed as a directly named style in the source collection.
visualIdentity: Explicit: turn-of-the-millennium digital optimism with chrome type, transparent plastic, rounded devices, early web elements, and bright accents. Material rules must stay coherent. Animation includes rotations, elastic reveals, and interface assembly, and metallic highlights must not overpower the message.
suitableUses: Explicit: the source lists product and editorial introductions, explanatory narratives, and abstract or cinematic sequences with meaningful chapters. Suggested examples include retro-themed app launches, campaign microsites, playful teasers, and social ads. Inferred: optimistic brand moments that rely on chrome and plastic.
limitations: Explicit: omit or adapt when the topic is too short for chapters, when transitions obscure causality, or when a cut violates a continuous-shot or loop requirement. Avoid metallic highlights that obscure the message and squashing text. Simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production. Example dimensions and aspect ratios are optional, and the source does not specify others.
palette: Status: an authored suggestion for new artwork only when no approved palette is supplied; task, brand, or reference colors override it. Tokens: background #E9EDF0, foreground #293341, accent_1 #7497D0, accent_2 #DB8CBB, accent_3 #A5C365. Gradients are disabled. Foreground on background measures 10.849:1. Accent_1 fails normal text at 4.306:1, so it is decorative only. Accent_2 and accent_3 pass with foreground at 5.158:1 and 6.443:1. Verify these pairs on composited frames.
motionAndInteraction: Explicit: animate rotations, elastic reveals, and interface assembly without letting highlights dominate. Shared guidance favors smooth, authored movement, but deliberate cuts, impacts, and reading holds should be preserved. Production guidance forbids adding springs or bounce automatically, so elasticity must be authored per element. Video state derives from composition time. Interactive delivery may add hover, keyboard, touch, and reduced-motion behavior.
audio: Unspecified in the source for this style. Audio should be proposed from the topic, audience, and motion, and may include music, voiceover, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence. No genre, tempo, instrument, or voice is assigned. Supplied audio requirements take priority. Speech must stay intelligible, clipping must be avoided, and picture-sync must be verified in the final video.
assetRequirements: Unspecified in the source for fonts, images, or models. The style needs chrome-finished type, transparent plastic objects, rounded device forms, and early web interface elements. Metallic type and plastic objects call for 3D materials, while interface elements use real DOM or SVG. Fonts and assets must load before rendering, and any missing asset must be reported rather than substituted silently.
combinations: Explicit suggestions: style-095 for interface assembly and state transitions, with functional buttons, visible focus, and Y2K styling. Style-106 for elastic squash-and-stretch on plastic objects, with volume preserved and one timing family. Avoid glassmorphism blur, and reserve chrome for one hero element. Motion patterns: motion-012, motion-015, and motion-020 list Y2K Design as a fit, while motion-014 fits only with an energy metaphor.
productionApproach: Explicit: HyperFrames is the default pipeline for composition timing, media sync, validation, and export. Remotion is a fallback only when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation exists, and that reason must be recorded. Three.js builds metallic and plastic 3D forms, while HTML/CSS and SVG render interface elements. Motion is optional, and the GSAP timeline serves as the framework clock. Reviewers must inspect key frames and watch the full video, including sync and loop continuity.
